chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Barqi, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Abu Saeed, from Al-Ahwal, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What is the lowest amount with which one can contract a Mut'ah marriage?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A handful of wheat.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum dower required for Mut'ah marriage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal principle of 'minimal sufficiency' (qalil) for the dower in temporary marriage, emphasizing that the validity of the contract does not depend on substantial wealth but on the mutual consent of the parties. By specifying a handful of wheat, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the accessibility of Mut'ah across all economic classes, a key distinction from permanent marriage where higher dowers are often customary. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the minimum threshold that prevents the contract from being void for lack of consideration.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed and Muhammad Bin Khalid Al Barqy, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Abu Saeed, from Al Ahowl who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘(What is) the lowest of what can be married with for the Mut’a?’ Heasws said: ‘A handful of wheat’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqiy from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhariy from abu Sa‘id from al-Ahwal who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the minimum amount of mahr (dower) in al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage).
He (the Imam) said, ‘It can be a handful of wheat.’”
